summary: Iter62 — AI-Assist validation + actual-resolution rules (shared core/ai_assess.py) verified end-to-end on the LIVE preview backend through BOTH flows: POST /api/decisions/{id}/factors/{fid}/ai-assess (My Dezider) and POST /api/pros-cons/{id}/factors/{fid}/ai-assess (Pros & Cons). 10/12 pytest cases PASS. All six validation rules behave exactly per spec on BOTH endpoints (Cases 1, 2, 3, 5 → 400 with correct message; Case 4 → 200 integer 0..100). The two failures (MD Case 6 + PC Case 6 — qualitative-with-AI-inferred-actual) are NOT a code defect: backend logs show the LLM call rejected with `litellm.BadRequestError: OpenAIException - Budget has been exceeded! Current cost: 0.42548 Max budget: 0.4`. The shared helper therefore correctly returns HTTP 502 'AI assessment unavailable — please enter % manually.' which is exactly the contract in core/ai_assess.py:456. As soon as EMERGENT_LLM_KEY budget is topped up, Case 6 on both flows will return 200 with `actual_value` AI-inferred. No 500 errors anywhere; no behavioural drift between the two flows. Exact 400 detail messages captured below in rca_of_issue.

minor.issue: Returns 502 'AI assessment unavailable — please enter % manually.' because EMERGENT_LLM_KEY OpenAI budget is exhausted (LiteLLM: 'Budget has been exceeded! Current cost: 0.42548, Max budget: 0.4'). The deterministic numeric-ratio fallback in core/ai_assess.py:_assess_pct does NOT apply to qualitative factors (no numeric expected/actual), so pct stays None and the route raises 502. Code is correct; environment/key budget needs a refill before Case 6 can return 200.

action_items: Top-up / reset the EMERGENT_LLM_KEY OpenAI budget (litellm reports Max budget: 0.4 already consumed) so qualitative AI-Assist (Case 6 in both flows) can run to completion and return the AI-inferred actual_value + percentage. NO code change required — core/ai_assess.py already returns the correct 502 contract on LLM failure.

After the budget refill, re-run only the two affected tests:  pytest backend/tests/test_iter62_ai_assess_validation.py::TestMDValidation::test_md_case6_qual_inferred_actual_200 backend/tests/test_iter62_ai_assess_validation.py::TestPCValidation::test_pc_case6_qual_inferred_actual_200 -v
critical_code_review_comments: core/ai_assess.py (466 lines) is well-structured single-source-of-truth — both routes consume `ai_assess_factor`. Parity guaranteed.

Quantitative deterministic fallback (lines 412-419) gracefully covers LLM outages for Case 4 (we observed it ran: budget was exhausted on the very first LLM call but Case 4 still returned 200 via ratio = 1200/1000 → 100%). Good defense-in-depth.

Qualitative path has NO non-LLM fallback. When LLM is down, Case 6 will always 502. If the product requirement is for AI-Assist to degrade gracefully on LLM-down for qualitative, consider returning a 200 with a neutral pct (e.g. 50) and source='ai_unavailable' OR documenting the 502 as the intentional 'please enter % manually' UX contract (frontend already handles this).

Pros & Cons response uses `assessment_pct` whereas My Dezider uses `percentage` for the same value (decisions.py:287 vs pros_cons.py:954). Both routes return `actual_value` consistently. The naming asymmetry is intentional per the review request, but flagging for future API-cleanup work.

success_rate.backend: 10/12 = 83% (the 2 failures are environment-bound: LLM budget exhausted, not code defects)

seed_data_creation: Module-scoped pytest fixtures created one TEST_iter62_md_{ts} decision (with two factors quant + qual + one option) AND one TEST_iter62_pc_{ts} pros-cons analysis (with one option + two factors). Both are auto-deleted on teardown (DELETE /api/decisions/{id} and DELETE /api/pros-cons/{id}).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Test file: /app/backend/tests/test_iter62_ai_assess_validation.py (uses admin@test.com — super@test.com falls through with 401 per credentials.md). The 6 validation rules are FULLY exercised on BOTH endpoints. Case 6 (qualitative inferred-actual) requires a working EMERGENT_LLM_KEY OpenAI budget; until that is restored, the 502 response is the correct contract. rca_of_issue:
Exact 400 detail strings captured during this run:
  • MD Case 1 (operator missing): 'AI Assist for the quantitative factor "Cost" needs an Operator (e.g. ≥). Set it in Step 5 (Review & Refine Expectations) and try again.'
  • MD Case 2 (expected missing): 'AI Assist for the quantitative factor "Cost" needs an Expected value. Set it in Step 5 …'
  • MD Case 3 (actual missing):   'AI Assist for the quantitative factor "Cost" needs an Actual value. Enter it, set a Data Source for the factor, or link this option to a Solution Store item so the value can be fetched.'
  • MD Case 5 (qual expected missing): 'AI Assist for the qualitative factor "Team culture" needs an Expected value to assess against. Set it in Step 5 …'
  • PC Cases 1/2/3/5 — identical messages (shared helper).
The 502 RCA for Cases 6: litellm.BadRequestError 'OpenAIException - Budget has been exceeded! Current cost: 0.42548, Max budget: 0.4'. Reproduce by hitting either endpoint with a qualitative factor (data_type='text') and expected_value set + no actual_value. Mitigation: refill EMERGENT_LLM_KEY OpenAI budget; no code change needed.
